title: I Used the Darkroom Chemical Log on the Mentor Who Poured My Tray

parts.text: I mixed developer at 7:33 p.m. and initialed the log: TRAY A, FRESH, 7:33, LEN. Mentor Pat poured my tray into a bottle labeled DEMO and waved me to the exhausted tank. The wall card said: SIGN THE LOG. DO NOT DUMP A FRESH TRAY. I was twenty-four, photo-club, holding a still-wet test strip. "Mentors are chemistry." I photographed the empty tray, the log, and the bottle. Then I logged a dump exception. At 7:41 the club chair asked why Pat's name was on my fresh tray. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The club chair can see Pat's demo bottle on my 7:33 fresh-tray log.

social.video_title: He poured my fresh tray into a demo bottle — Part 1/2
social.description: Darkroom, a wet test strip, and a wall card the mentor posted. I logged the dump. Would you have photographed the bottle?

parts.text: Pat called it teaching until the chair asked for the log. I printed the exception, the photo, and the card. Chemistry remixed tray A. Pat mixed his own demo and told beginners dumps were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when a bottle exists. The log now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE TRAY. I keep my initials. Pat labels demo from the start. The room finally smells like developer, not a shortcut. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the tray — Part 2/2
social.description: Exception, remixed chemistry, and a second line. Was teaching ever my test strip?
